To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) H/WQ models are used for technical, policy and legal decision-making, and therefore the methods used and the decisions made should be documented and reported, and (2), H/WQ modeling studies should be fully reproducible.

(1) the eight elements of model documentation described herein provide a comprehensive and consistent framework for reporting the calibration, validation, use, and limitations of H/WQ simulation models and that (2) a shift toward full reproducibility of model calibration, validation and use is desirable and will lead to better understanding of model performance, improved model development, and more effective use of models in decision making.

the following eight elements should be included in H/WQ model documentation and reporting: (1) model description, (2) model inputs, (3) model calibration, (4) model validation, (5) model application, (6) model results, (7) model limitations, and (8) model uncertainty.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) the documentation and reporting procedures used in the calibration, validation, application and use of H/WQ modeling, (2) the development of guidelines and recommendations to improve the documentation and reporting of these activities, (3) the development and use of model documentation and reproducible research tools to facilitate the documentation and reporting process, and (4) the development and implementation of model documentation and use guidelines in the H/WO modeling community.
